notes: Created mobile responsiveness implementation plan after @world-review analysis of 5 reported issues: (1) two-finger pan inverted on phone, (2) one-finger scroll blocked by touch-action:none, (3) canvas overflows viewport bottom, (4) cramped layout below 700px, (5) landscape mode insufficient. Plan has 3 phases: P0 Touch Gesture Fixes (negate TouchEvent pan delta for direct manipulation convention, change touch-action from none to pan-y), P1 Responsive CSS Layout (700px breakpoint, sidebar overlays, full-width canvas), P2 Mobile Polish (safe areas, touch targets). Key technical finding: TouchEvent pan uses direct manipulation convention (drag right = image moves right) while WheelEvent uses scrolling convention (scroll down = view moves down) — these are opposite and the TouchEvent delta needs negation. Canvas touch-action:none blocks all default touch gestures; changing to pan-y allows one-finger vertical scroll while preserving two-finger gesture interception via preventDefault().
